name: Enjin CryptoItems ERC-1538 registry adapter initialize manager takeover
summary: The two Enjin ERC-1538 adapter registries route every registered adapter selector through their own fallback, including the adapter template's initialize(uint256). Called directly on a registry, that initializer runs in registry storage, where its once-only guard slot was never set and its owner slot is the registry's pending-manager slot. Any caller could therefore make itself pending manager and accept management. The attacker took over both registries and pointed the item-adapter transfer selectors at its own code. It then pulled ERC-1155 items from holders without approval and melted them, draining 6.58M ENJ of backing from the platform reserve.
notes: The manager's updateContract call emitted FunctionUpdate(bytes4,address,address,string) for selector 0xfe4b84df (initialize(uint256)). It routed that selector on registry A from 0x0 to the ERC-721 adapter template 0x24591e79, making the unguarded initializer reachable in registry storage. It is the only pre-exploit FunctionUpdate for that selector; the registry runtime (block 13530687) and the template (block 13530845) are older.

FunctionUpdate for selector 0xfe4b84df (initialize(uint256)) routed that selector on registry B from 0x0 to the ERC-20 adapter template 0x75512f84. It is the only pre-exploit FunctionUpdate for that selector; the registry runtime (block 13530678) and the template (block 13530836) are older.

Gross reserve depletion across 595 attacker transactions (blocks 25834071-25834993). Stolen items were melted for 6,518,518.5545533333333333 ENJ paid to the attack contract, plus 61,108.67468 ENJ the reserve paid to 22 other recipients inside the same melt calls (not deducted). The anchor transaction alone melted 5,231,353 ENJ to the attacker. Value of stolen items that were not melted is not measured. The attacker's later ENJ swaps do not set the valuation.
Sibling registry exploited in the same anchor transaction; its initialize route was installed at block 13530886, two blocks before target-1's (13530888), so target-1 carries the knot.
